o.text: From Proto-Turkic *öl- (“to die”). Cognate with Turkish ölmek, Kazakh өлу (ölüw, “to die”), Uzbek oʻlmoq (“to die”), etc.

From Proto-Turkic *čẹr (“rotten, foul; to rot; illness; dirt; to be sick, ill; rot; glue; anguish, sorrow”)
whence also Azerbaijani çürümək (“to rot”); alternatively from Persian چرک (čerk). However, it has been proposed that the latter Persian term is a Turkic borrowing itself (ibid.).
From Proto-Turkic *beŋiŕ (“face; to be similar; open forestless place on a mountain slope”). Equivalent to bəniz + -ə.
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *semri- (“to fatten”). Doublet of səmizmək.
From Arabic تَبَدُّلَات (tabaddulāt), plural of تَبَدُّل (tabaddul).
